title: Batch jobs moved to a new region can't install dependencies
intro: To cut latency, the batch workers were moved from us-east1 to europe-west1 using the same instance template (no external IPs, 'for security'). In europe-west1 every job fails at 'pip install' with 'Connection timed out'. The same template works fine in us-east1.

steps.prompt: Read recent error logs from Compute Engine VMs (last hour, 10 entries).
steps.fake_output:
textPayload: 'batch-ew1-7k2m: pip: Connection to pypi.org timed out. (connect timeout=15)'
textPayload: 'batch-ew1-9q4n: pip: Connection to pypi.org timed out. (connect timeout=15)'
steps.hint: Filter by resource type and severity.

steps.prompt: Private VMs need Cloud NAT to reach the internet, and NAT is regional. List the Cloud Routers.
steps.fake_output:
NAME          REGION    NETWORK
router-use1   us-east1  prod-vpc
steps.hint: Cloud NAT is configured on a Cloud Router, per region.

steps.prompt: Only us-east1 has a router, and its NAT. Create router-ew1 on prod-vpc in europe-west1.
expected_commands: gcloud compute routers create router-ew1 --network prod-vpc --region europe-west1

steps.prompt: Add NAT config nat-ew1 to router-ew1 (europe-west1) with auto-allocated IPs for all subnet ranges.
expected_commands: gcloud compute routers nats create nat-ew1 --router router-ew1 --region europe-west1 --auto-allocate-nat-external-ips --nat-all-subnet-ip-ranges
gcloud compute routers nats create nat-ew1 --router=router-ew1 --region=europe-west1 --auto-allocate-nat-external-ips --nat-all-subnet-ip-ranges

steps.prompt: Verify from one worker, batch-ew1-7k2m in europe-west1-b, through IAP: run 'curl -sI https://pypi.org | head -1'.
expected_commands: gcloud compute ssh batch-ew1-7k2m --zone europe-west1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command 'curl -sI https://pypi.org | head -1'
gcloud compute ssh batch-ew1-7k2m --zone=europe-west1-b --tunnel-through-iap --command="curl -sI https://pypi.org | head -1"

resolution: In GCP the VPC is global but Cloud NAT is regional. The instance template was fine: its VMs had no external IPs, which is correct. But egress for private VMs only works in regions where a Cloud Router with a NAT configuration exists, and nobody created one for europe-west1. The network-wide default route to the internet gateway looks like it should work, but it only carries traffic for VMs that have an external IP. 'Same template, different region, different result' points at a regional resource. Prevention: put router and NAT creation in the same Terraform module that 'enables a region', so a region can't be half set up. Private Google Access would also let the workers pull from Artifact Registry without NAT, but public package indexes like PyPI still need NAT, or better, a mirror in Artifact Registry.
